messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PROD alert: GPU scheduling backlog growing in cluster prod-ml. Pending GPU pods >300, queue growth steady for 8m. See: https://console.metrics/prod-ml/queues

oncall-sre: I'm awake, grabbing it. Paging SRE rotation and Eng-Infra.

Marta (SRE): looking at k8s events and CA logs now. `kubectl get pods --field-selector=status.phase=Pending -n infra-gpu` shows a lot in Pending with "0/0 nodes are available".

Raj (Eng-Infra): preliminary look at ASG scs-gpu-pool. Desired = 40, max = 40. ASG at cap. Suspect scale-up blocked.

Marta (SRE): cluster-autoscaler logs showing repeated errors when trying to create instances:
```
W0312 03:05:12.123456 1 aws_manager.go:512] aws: request failed: InvalidParameter: Launch Template version 'lt-2025-omega' does not exist
status code: 400, request id: 9f3a-xxxx
```
So CA attempted a launch template version we don't have in that ASG.

Raj (Eng-Infra): aha — CI rolled a new LT version in eu-west-1 but the ASG in prod-ml still references the older version due to a failed rollout. Also I see some recent IAM changes: instance profile name changed from `redwood-gpu-role` -> `redwood-gpu-role-v2`. ASG still uses old profile. That would block instance creation.

Marta (SRE): also seeing some AWS API rate limit errors in the last 10m: `Throttling: Rate exceeded`. Could be making scale attempts noisy and CA backing off.

Eli (Customer Success): customers reporting 429s and slow embeddings jobs. CS queue backlog increased, some jobs expired. Impacting Dedicated customers in eu-west-1, tagging `acct-*` and `partner-infra`. I'm filing incident emails.

oncall-sre: quick mitigation options?

Raj (Eng-Infra): short-term manual interventions: 1) bump ASG max to allow CA to satisfy pending pods (but if LT/instance profile mismatch remains, instances will fail) 2) revert ASG to known-working LT version 3) create temporary emergency ASG using fallback launch template that still works. I can do (1)+(2) if approved.

Nina (Product): prioritize minimal customer impact. If a manual bump gets capacity up quickly, do it. We can schedule a rollback of the LT deploy after.

Marta (SRE): executing triage steps now:
- Checking recent LT/ASG changes `aws autoscaling describe-launch-configurations` & `aws ec2 describe-launch-templates --launch-template-ids ...`
- Fetching CA decision logs `kubectl -n kube-system logs deploy/cluster-autoscaler`

deploy-bot: Deployment pipeline note: recent infra rollout `infra/gpu/launch-template` completed 22m ago (commit d4c3). Manual rollback option available: `ci rollback infra/gpu/launch-template --to-tag v1.13`

Raj (Eng-Infra): I'll prepare the rollback but will first attempt to hotfix the ASG instance profile binding — small risk. If anyone objects speak now.

Eli (Customer Success): please do. Customers are hitting timeouts. Send a status update once we have a temporary capacity plan.

Marta (SRE): running these commands now:
```
aws autoscaling update-auto-scaling-group --auto-scaling-group-name scs-gpu-pool --max-size 60
aws autoscaling attach-instances-profile --instance-profile-name redwood-gpu-role-v2 --auto-scaling-group-name scs-gpu-pool
```
(Will post results)

~2 minutes later~

Marta (SRE): first command accepted, max-size bumped to 60. Second call returned `Error: InstanceProfileNotFound: InstanceProfile redwood-gpu-role-v2 not found` — seems the IAM change hasn't propagated or the name was different. Rolling back plan B: create emergency ASG using fallback LT.

Raj (Eng-Infra): creating emergency-asg-gpu-fallback using LT v1.13 and profile `redwood-gpu-role`. Spinning up 8 nodes as a fast path.

Marta (SRE): CA picked up the new nodes as they registered, but new nodes are tainted `gpu=dedicated:NoSchedule`. Our pods need that taint tolerated. Checking pod tolerations.

Marta (SRE): many workload pods don't have the toleration — they rely on nodeSelector + resource request. I'm patching a DaemonSet that adds tolerations via mutating webhook? Too risky. Easier: temporarily remove the taint from the new nodes while we patch workloads.

Raj (Eng-Infra): removing taint from emergency nodes now: `kubectl taint nodes node-xyz gpu=dedicated:NoSchedule-`

Marta (SRE): pods are scheduling onto fallback nodes. Queue drain rate improving. Monitoring token-level latency.

Eli (Customer Success): getting reports that throttles are decreasing, some jobs completed. I'll update the affected customers and advise the workaround.

Nina (Product): thanks. Once stabilized, we need a postmortem: why LT deployment and IAM change didn't validate the ASG state. Also add a canary to prevent hitting ASG at max.

Marta (SRE): next steps: 1) keep emergency ASG running while we reconcile LT and instance profile, 2) revert/migrate ASG to use the working LT v1.13 or ensure rollout completes with CI, 3) add CA retry/backoff tuning for AWS throttles, 4) document runbook gaps.

Raj (Eng-Infra): I'll coordinate rollback of LT and recreate instance profile alias. Also file ticket to add automated validation in pipeline that checks running ASGs before LT promotion.

oncall-sre: handing off to night rotation: Marta will stay on for next 30m then hand to next on-call. If any regressions, page #oncall immediately.

Marta (SRE): leaving detailed notes in the incident channel and creating an incident tracker. Current status: capacity restored via emergency ASG, queue trending down, customer impact reduced but not fully cleared (some timeouts). Last checked: 03:24Z.

Eli (Customer Success): posting customer-facing status: "We are experiencing degraded performance for GPU jobs in eu-west-1. Mitigation in progress; new capacity added. ETA to full recovery 1h."

Nina (Product): good. Capture exact affected customer list for SRE/CS review.

Marta (SRE): creating post-incident checklist and will attach CA logs, ASG events, and commands used. Handoff complete.

oncall-sre: closing pager, follow-up tasks assigned. :white_check_mark:
